name: mcp-books
description: MCP server that searches the Internet Archive and the Library of Congress at once, inside scanned text and across catalogues. No API key required.
long_description:
Ask where a phrase was ever printed, and two archives answer at once: the Internet Archive, holding the machine-read text of digitised books, periodicals and documents, and the Library of Congress, holding the text of American newspaper pages. The corpora are different bodies of material, so the answer is the two put together rather than one question asked twice.

What makes the merge usable is what it refuses to flatten. A page number is a real leaf on the archive whose index holds one and null on the archive whose index holds none, and no page is ever invented. An excerpt says what it is: the passage that matched, or the opening of a page sent because the searched words sit further down than the text that came back, and the answer counts how many are openings. Counts are reported in each archive's own terms and never added, because one counts documents and the other counts leaves. Terms of reuse are stated per record, and a record stating none has granted nothing.

An archive that fails is named, with the moment that failed. An archive that cannot answer a question is named as absent, with the reason, rather than quietly left out.

tools.description: Find a phrase in the machine-read text of every archive at once.
